text:
Asha: Heads up — Zenora onboarding flagged. Their staging traffic showed p95 jumps ~350–450ms and token cost is higher than expected. Renewal health moved to 'monitor'. Need quick, low-risk ops recs (quant/model/routing) before our Tuesday call. @Diego @Liam
Diego: Quick read — sounds like a candidate for a compact int8 model + routing to a dedicated pool for hot paths. We can canary a compact int8 variant that tends to cut CPU and latency ~20–30% on similar workloads. Suggest 10% traffic canary first.
Emma: Agree. Also enable prefix/KV caching for their short-chat flows and reduce kv_cache TTL to 30s for faster hits. Turn on continuous batching with a conservative max_batch_tokens=1024 to keep tail latency predictable.
Liam: Dedicated eu-west pool has spare GPUs but not a ton during business hours. We can reserve a single node for the canary and set a strict capacity cap so other tenants aren't affected. We'll also need a fallback to hosted compact if the dedicated pool saturates.
Diego: Proposed routing + quant policy snippet (canary):
```yaml
routing_policies:
  - name: zenora-canary-high-priority
    match_headers:
      x-customer-tier: zenora
      x-traffic-seg: hot
    target: dedicated-eu-west-zenora
    canary_percentage: 10
    fallback: hosted-compact-int8-v2
quantization:
  prefer_model: redwood-compact-int8-v2
  per_route_overrides:
    - route: zenora-canary-high-priority
      q_config: int8
```
Diego: Canary should reduce p95 and CPU cost; fallback keeps requests flowing if capacity hits limits.
Asha: Good. What's the rollback plan if quality degrades? We need a quick switch-off and evaluation metric.
Emma: Keep the canary short (2 hours) and run the customer eval suite continuously. Track: p95 latency, 95/99 token cost, error rate, and a quality score computed from their eval prompts (exact-match / semantic-f1). If quality delta > 3% we revert.
Liam: I'll add infra safeguards: auto-cap the dedicated pool at 50% for this canary and enforce circuit-breaker to route to fallback after 3 consecutive 503s or latency > 700ms for 2 minutes.
ops-bot: Scheduled: zenora-canary-deploy at 2026-03-23T18:00:00Z. Notifying oncall.
Asha: Action items: Diego — set up canary config + rollout (ETA 3h). Liam — confirm capacity/reserve node and add circuit-breaker (ETA 2h). Emma — wire eval prompts & monitoring dashboard (ETA 4h). I'll message Zenora with the proposed low-risk window.
Diego: On it. Will push config to staging and open PR with runbook steps.
Liam: Reserved one node and set capacity cap; will post instance id in the PR. Also adding alert rules.
ops-bot: Alert created: zenora-canary-latency-alert -> trigger if p95 > 400ms for 5m.
Emma: Dashboard done: p95, p99, error rate, token cost per request, quality delta. Also hooked the eval suite to CI so we get continuous quality reports during canary.
Asha: Perfect — thanks team :thumbsup: I'll brief CS lead and schedule a 15m post-canary check-in. If the canary looks stable we'll expand to 50% traffic before full swap.
Diego: Small note — if we see hallucination drift on a subset of prompts, we should fallback to the full-precision compact model instead of the int8 until we diagnose.
Asha: Noted. Will add that to the runbook.
Emma: I'll add a short checklist for the CS team to collect customer feedback during the 2-hour window (sample prompts, UX notes).
Asha: Great — closing this thread for now, will ping updates in the next hour.
